title: Run a privacy-safe beta or dogfood cohort for deliver linked screen and diagram editing
summary: Expose a bounded cohort to the current product, collect only necessary evidence, protect privacy, and decide whether the experience is ready to expand.
acceptance_criteria: Define a bounded beta or dogfood cohort for `internal visual product, design, diagram, and proposal workspace` and the journey `open repository-backed design truth, place screens and diagram objects, select and transform them, connect flows, inspect source context, and save`.
State cohort eligibility, size, duration, version, platform, locale, device, and exclusion criteria.
Define opt-in, consent, privacy, telemetry, support, and withdrawal before exposure.
Use feature flags or configuration only where they have owner, default, kill switch, and stale-state posture.
Record eligible, exposed, activated, first-value, meaningful-value, repeated-value, support-needed, opted-out, and unavailable states separately.
Do not infer success from install, availability, or lack of complaints.
Define product, safety, privacy, accessibility, performance, support, and monetization guardrails.
Define stop, rollback, pause, and escalation conditions.
Collect only the minimum event and diagnostic data needed for the decision.
Keep event names, properties, purpose, sensitivity, retention, and owners in a versioned contract.
Provide manual or local evidence paths for products that intentionally avoid analytics.
Handle offline event buffering, deduplication, clock drift, version changes, and consent withdrawal.
Provide support entry and known-issue communication for participants.
Separate participant feedback from observed product behavior.
Track environment and external-service blockers independently from product defects.
Review evidence at a predefined cadence rather than waiting for the end.
Preserve previous cohort and configuration history through supersession.
Do not expand the cohort or enable production monetization automatically.
Produce proposed findings and a go, change, pause, or stop recommendation.
Record sample-size and selection-bias limitations.
Validate telemetry, flags, rollback, and privacy behavior.
Finish with zero app-owned warnings.

agent_notes: Portfolio Human Validation & Product Launch Wave 13.
Non-scope: do not release, deploy, sign, publish, enable billing or ads, operate hardware, write NAS data, migrate users, merge products, or create future game repositories.
Alternative considered and rejected: relying on internal confidence, green builds, or download counts without observed user or operator value would create false product certainty.
Research, telemetry, and feedback must remain privacy-safe, versioned, and optional where the product role requires it.

Final Wave 14 validity review: `valid-after-sudoku`; publication `publish-as-proposed-backlog`; implementation sequence `after-sudoku`. Human validation remains valuable after the product implementation prerequisites and Sudoku priority.
